text:
Jin Park: Quick follow-up from the runtime probe I ran this morning across A100/H100/L4 on branch runtime/opt-kernels. Found a small-but-consistent perf anomaly on L4 when we hit the mixed-precision tiled-attn path.

Marie Gomez: can you paste the minimal repro and perf numbers?

Jin Park: repro is the usual lm concat workload (seq=1024, bs=8) using bfloat16 for model weights, but we forced the tiled kernel by setting KERNEL_PREF=tiling in the env. Numbers:
```
A100: 13.2 ms/token (tiling, bf16)
H100: 12.8 ms/token (tiling, bf16)
L4: 18.6 ms/token (tiling, bf16)
L4 (fp16 path): 11.5 ms/token
```
So L4 falls back or runs a slower code path for bf16 tiled case, but runs fast on fp16.

Alex Chen: hmm that suggests our bf16 kernel selection logic is mis-detecting SM capability on L4. We currently gate bf16-tiled on sm_capability>=SM_FEATURE_MMA_BF16 and a separate tiling_support flag. Any chance L4 reports those differently in the CUDA/driver probe?

Jin Park: I dumped the capability probe results from runtime probe tool:
```
GPU: L4
sm_version: 86
reported_features: [mma_fp16, sparse, tensorcore_mma_fp16]
probe_flags: {bf16_avail: false, tiling_hw: true}
```
So probe says bf16_avail=false. But NV driver docs indicate L4 does bf16 via fp16 pathways; it's not native bf16 MMA like H100. Our kernel selection currently treats bf16_avail=false as "must avoid bf16-optimized kernels" which pushes to a generic emulation path that is slower.

Sri Patel: Could be a mismatch between driver VIR/ABI and our probe heuristics. L4 sometimes advertises bfloat via operator-level support not via tensor core feature bits. We should detect bf16-friendly fp16 paths separately and not rigidly require bf16_avail.

Marie Gomez: Agreed. For short term, maybe add a special-case for L4 family: if sm_version in [86] and tiling_hw==true and fp16_tensorcore==true then allow bf16-tiling kernel that uses fp16 intrinsics with conversion?

Alex Chen: That will work but we also need to ensure numerical parity tests. The fp16-emulation-for-bf16 kernel has slightly different rounding. Add a canary eval with the standard prompts to check delta < 1e-3 on logprobs.

Jin Park: I ran canary eval on a 200-example prompt set. Delta mean abs logprob: 2.1e-4, max 9.3e-4. Passes our 1e-3 threshold but close to cusp.

devops-bot: deploy requested: rollout group=canary group_size=10% target=dedicated-l4-pool-3 by=2026-03-21T09:00Z

Marie Gomez: For longer term, we should revisit probe granularity. Proposal: separate physical BF16 tensorcore support vs bf16-via-fp16 emulation. Update probe API: add field bf16_emulated: true/false, and kernel metadata accept_emulated_bf16: true/false.

Alex Chen: I can submit a small RFC for the probe change. Also suggest adding an opt-in runtime flag: RUNTIME_ALLOW_BF16_EMULATED=1 so we can gate rollout across customers.

Sri Patel: One more thing — crossover case when quantized INT8 kernels exist. L4 has excellent INT8 throughput; our routing currently prefers bf16-tiling if model supports it. For some workloads INT8 + dequant backend is cheaper and faster. We should add cost-model comparisons rather than hard preference.

Jin Park: noted. Action items:
- Alex: RFC for probe fields (bf16_emulated) + RUNTIME_ALLOW_BF16_EMULATED flag.
- Marie: small kernel patch that accepts emulated bf16 on L4 family and unit tests for numerical delta.
- Sri: quick cost-model doc for auto-routing bf16 vs int8 on L4.
- Jin: run canary rollout once patch + flag ready and report perf+quality.

Marie Gomez: I'll aim to have the kernel patch + unit tests by EOD tomorrow.

Alex Chen: RFC PR opened: github.com/redwood/runtime/pulls/1723 — feedback welcome.

Jin Park: thanks all. If anyone wants the raw probe logs, ping me and I'll drop them. :thumbsup:

Alex Chen: pinged you for logs, thx.

Sri Patel: small note — let's add a short line in release notes about L4 bf16 behavior so SREs don't get paged for perf regressions during deploys.

Jin Park: will add to the rollout checklist.
